title: 2026 Texas Gubernatorial Election
description: The 2026 Texas gubernatorial election will be held on November 3, 2026, to elect the governor of Texas. Incumbent Republican Governor Greg Abbott is seeking a fourth term after easily winning his party's March 2026 primary with 82% of the vote. He will face Democratic nominee Gina Hinojosa, a state representative from Austin who won a competitive nine-way Democratic primary with approximately 59% of the vote, as well as Libertarian nominee Pat Dixon and independent candidate Jenn Mack Raphoon. The race is being closely watched as Abbott aims to become the longest-serving governor in Texas history, while Hinojosa seeks to become the first Democrat elected governor of Texas since 1990. Key issues include public education funding and school vouchers, border security, property taxes, and energy grid reliability.
polling_note: Multiple polls conducted from February through May 2026 show Greg Abbott leading Gina Hinojosa by margins ranging from 3 to 7 percentage points, with Abbott consistently polling in the high 40s and Hinojosa in the low-to-mid 40s. Some polls do not include third-party or independent candidates.

candidates.name: Greg Abbott
candidates.summary: Greg Abbott has served as the 48th Governor of Texas since 2015, previously serving as Texas Attorney General (2002-2015) and as a Justice on the Texas Supreme Court. Born in Wichita Falls and raised in Duncanville, he earned a BBA from the University of Texas at Austin and a JD from Vanderbilt University Law School. Abbott is running for a fourth term on a platform emphasizing border security, property tax reform, school choice, and economic growth, having been named one of Time magazine's 100 Most Influential People in 2024.

candidates.name: Gina Hinojosa
candidates.summary: Gina Hinojosa is a Texas State Representative from the 49th district (2017-present) and the Democratic nominee for governor. Born in McAllen and raised in Brownsville, she earned a BA from the University of Texas at Austin and a JD from George Washington University Law School, then worked as a civil rights and labor lawyer. Hinojosa previously served on the Austin ISD school board from 2012 to 2016, including as board president, and is running on a platform focused on public education funding, healthcare access, affordability, and government accountability.

candidates.name: Pat Dixon
candidates.summary: Pat Dixon is the Libertarian Party nominee for Texas Governor. A former two-term Lago Vista City Council member (2005-2010), he served 10 years as Chair of the Libertarian Party of Texas and two terms on the Libertarian National Committee. Born in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania, Dixon attended Miami University in Ohio where he studied engineering, and later worked for Honeywell and as President of DPAS Inc., an industrial automation consulting firm. He is also the author of 'Leading Like a Libertarian' and 'Primary Screenout.'

candidates.name: Jenn Mack Raphoon
candidates.summary: Jenn Mack Raphoon is an independent candidate for Texas Governor. A 7th-generation Texan, she describes herself as not a career politician and has a background in business and operations management. Raphoon is running on a platform emphasizing constitutional government, border security, and returning power to the people, positioning herself as an alternative to both major parties. She declared her candidacy for the 2026 general election as an independent.
